speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You are an infant presenting with recurrent stridor and wheezing; since you cannot speak for yourself, I will ask your caregivers questions. To begin, have these symptoms been triggered by specific activities like feeding, crying, or exertion, and do they occur only when lying down?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia with associated Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD). The symptoms of stridor worsening with neck flexion, crying, and feeding, alongside post-prandial vomiting, are highly characteristic of this condition.
